processes.description: Outside groups approach the West desk with proposed hourly-ahead or real-time power price indexes. The desk lead forwards each proposal, with the index definition and its template, to colleagues and asks for their feedback, then says which index he would take part in, provided it works. A round is the review of a proposal rather than a routine transaction.
steps: An outside group approaches the desk with a proposed hourly-ahead or real-time index for the West, with its definition and template.
The desk lead forwards the proposal to colleagues and asks them to review it and the template.
Colleagues review the definition and template and send their feedback.
The desk lead decides which index to participate in, provided it works.

automation.approach: A short evaluation checklist for each proposed index could record its definition, the delivery points and periods it covers, what the desk would submit and when, the template's format, who reviewed it and the participation decision, so competing proposals are compared on the same terms.
automation.rationale: The work is occasional and rests on judgement about whether an index will work; the mail shows several groups proposing similar indexes and the desk lead asking colleagues for feedback. A checklist keeps those reviews consistent and records why the desk joins a particular index and not another.

processes.description: The real-time desk lead briefs the desk by email on what it needs on shift: links to transmission maps and the proposed OASIS, new and updated pages for the desk's information packet, BPA transmission prices from the start of October, handling rules such as logging out of the IPC website and not filling EnMax sales with MPC energy, how to report outages, market changes heading into winter, and forwarded counterparty feedback on the desk's performance.
steps: The desk lead collects new information: transmission links and prices, rule changes, outage procedures or counterparty feedback.
He sends a briefing to the real-time desk, sometimes asking staff to print material such as a colour transmission map.
New and updated pages are added to the desk's information packet.
Staff apply the rules on shift, such as logging out of the IPC website and filling sales only with the right energy.
Outages are written up in an outage report sent to the Generation Outage Desk, with the Services Desk liaising with the outage desks.

stalls.summary: A new screen shown to the desk is only partly working: the ticker works and little else does.
The IPC website locks the desk out when a session times out, so staff have to remember to log out after each use.

contradictions.summary: The same reply has the real-time desk filling out an outage report and sending it to the Generation Outage Desk, while naming the Services Desk as responsible for communicating with both the Generation and Real Time Outage Desks, leaving unclear who contacts the Generation Outage Desk.

automation.approach: Keep the desk information packet as a single maintained document organised by topic (transmission paths and prices, outage reporting, counterparty handling rules, system access and log-out rules, seasonal market notes), with each entry dated from when it takes effect, so a briefing becomes an update to the packet plus a short notice pointing to it.
automation.rationale: The briefings are standing rules the desk must follow on every shift, but they arrive as separate emails that staff must find and sometimes print. A single written procedure keeps the current rule in a known place, makes superseded prices and rules visible, and gives new staff a single document to read.

processes.description: The real-time desk keeps each day's power schedules, imports and exports matched to the booked deals and to what the ISO and counterparties show. A round starts when the desk lead or a scheduler finds the desk long or short in a zone, a wrong schedule or import ID, a derated or cut path, or a counterparty limit. The email says what to buy or sell and for which book, which Enpower deals to enter, reprice or zero out, which tags and inc-sheet entries to complete, and whom to call, such as the CAISO, El Paso Electric or the preschedulers.
steps: The desk lead or a scheduler spots a long or short position, a wrong import or export, or a transmission derate or cut.
The position is checked against the schedule sheets, the Enpower deal entries and the ISO's records such as CAPS.
Traders buy or sell to fill the position, or arrange lending with El Paso Electric, for the book and price the email names.
Deals are entered, repriced or zeroed out in Enpower and deal scheduling, including cut schedules and the value of cut deals.
Tags and tag numbers go into the inc sheet and the EPE schedule sheet, tagged for both light and heavy load.
The desk calls the CAISO or the counterparty to confirm or change the schedule and summarises each deal in Pacific time.
Revenue from corrected deals is routed to the group that captures it, such as volume management.
The previous day's printed dispatch and prescheduling sheet are filed in the agreed folder for follow-up.

stalls.summary: The CAISO's systems fail during checkout: its computers go down and it again has difficulty reading the desk's bids, so schedules wait or have to be confirmed another way.

Schedule sheets carry errors that send rounds back for correction: a duplicate schedule in a sheet prepared ahead of the weekend, a wrong SPS volume, a wrong import ID, a period missing from the inc sheet, and an EPE schedule sheet that for yet another day leaves out schedules.

Deal entries are corrected after the fact: an El Paso Electric deal price is changed, a deal is zeroed out for part of the day, and a new deal summary shows revenue its writer says he should not receive.
Records that are lost or out of step have to be rebuilt: staff on shift must coordinate which deals were done and reconstruct a sheet, and a mismatch has to be squared away with the preschedulers.
Cut deals stay in the systems: the instruction to zero out cut deals in Enpower and value them is repeated later in capitals for deal scheduling.

The same procedures are restated in reminders, such as putting the tag number in the inc sheet, tagging both light and heavy load including the Southwest, and stating the Pacific time zone in deal summaries, which suggests these steps are often missed.
Short positions can be hard to fill: the desk reports asking every counterparty in the Northwest to sell it energy.
Follow-up work is put off to the next day when the desk lead has no time for it.

contradictions.summary: For the same schedule the desk expected a non-firm export, while CAPS showed a final firm import of the same size.

Volumes in the schedule records disagree with what was agreed: the SPS schedule shows a larger figure than it should for a delivery period, and an import ID carries the wrong on-peak and off-peak volumes.

After a deal price was changed, the new deal summary credits its writer with revenue he says he should not receive, while elsewhere revenue from a CAISO sale is said to go to the volume management group with no access for the real-time desk.

Different people are named for El Paso Electric schedule details: Kate as the source of prices and deal numbers for EPE lending, later Diane Cutsforth as working on the EPE schedule, while the previous day's EPE sheets still go to Kate Symes' old desk.

automation.approach: A checkout report could compare Enpower deal entries, the inc and EPE schedule sheets, the tags and the ISO's final schedules for each delivery period, flagging long or short positions, wrong import IDs or volumes, missing tag numbers and cut schedules not yet zeroed out. Traders would still decide what to buy or sell, call the ISO and counterparties, and value cut deals. A shift checklist would carry the recurring rules the desk lead keeps restating.
automation.rationale: The mail repeats the same reminders (tag numbers in the inc sheet, light and heavy load tags, Pacific time in deal summaries, zeroing out cut deals, filing the previous day's sheets) and shows errors that a routine check would catch before the ISO or a scheduler does. A shift checklist can be used straight away; the reconciliation report removes the manual comparison over time.

work_estimate.rationale: Most rounds centre on a single position or schedule: checking it against the schedule sheets, Enpower and the ISO's records, buying or selling to fill it, entering, repricing or zeroing the deal, updating the inc or EPE sheet and tags, and calling the ISO or counterparty. That is about 20 minutes; a plain notice of a position is nearer 10, while valuing cut deals or reconstructing a lost sheet runs toward 60. A reconciliation check could take over comparing deal entries, sheets, tags and ISO finals; buying, calling and judging cuts stay with people.
